title: A two-term complex with flat term in degree zero represents the truncated base change of its derived object
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement fixes an object K of D(R) whose cohomology is concentrated in degrees -1 and 0, chooses a two-term complex K^{-1} -> K^0 representing it with K^0 flat, and asserts that the naive tensor product complex K^bullet tensor_R R' represents the truncation in degrees at least -1 of the derived base change (statement lines 22519-22527). The proof is a comparison of distinguished triangles rather than a computation: the base-changed triangle has the derived tensor products, the second triangle has the naive tensor products, the comparison map between them has isomorphisms on the two outer vertices precisely because K^0 is flat, and the remaining input is that the lowest term K^{-1} agrees with its derived tensor product in degree 0 (proof lines 22530-22549). The non-routine part is knowing which truncation is obtained, which is what the careful reading of the second triangle in degrees at least -1 provides. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
